scenarios: a trusted MCP server is started lazily and its declaration parsed under the host's bounds and namespaced external.<server>.<tool>

a hostile server's forged native name, unusable name, oversize schema, 40-deep schema, off-machine $ref, escape-sequence description, smuggled requiredCapabilities/systemPrompt/effectClass and 200 tools are each refused or bounded while its good tools stand
a host-declared read runs under the lease; an undeclared tool is an external side effect held behind an intent-bound approval and only then reaches the real server
arguments are checked against the server's own declared schema before anything is sent
a call that outlives the host's patience is cancelled on the wire with notifications/cancelled naming the same request id
a server that exits mid-call leaves an effectful call EXTERNAL_OUTCOME_UNKNOWN
the server's own record of a call carries the session, task and call id the Core logged
a proposed-but-untrusted server is never started and never callable
external.call is excluded from the reviewer projection and absent from the review_isolated lease while external.list stays available
proof: the real modbit-core binary drives real MCP server processes over real pipes speaking the real protocol; the servers' own logs are read back to correlate what they were asked with what the Core logged.
audit: ABSENT before: nothing in the product spoke MCP (no matrix family, unread mcp_servers config layers, docs/17 listing the hub's surface as unbuilt).
limitations: stdio transport only; server configuration from MODBIT_MCP_SERVERS at boot (layered config and conversational management are IMP-EV-0128/0224); media parts typed but not yet routed through the Media Pipeline (IMP-EV-0187); tools/list pagination bounded and list_changed not acted on.
